scope: M4.2 hardening only: legacy keystore fallback, compare-and-replace rotation, monotonic registry revision, session replacement at capacity, lifecycle sweep scope, real registry-commit failure injection, wire-replay evidence field semantics, full-project test evidence, manifest and document cleanup. No benchmark, M5 not started.
single_writer_scope: trusted admin control plane is single-writer across processes; there is no file lock, so concurrent cross-process registry updates are NOT claimed to be safe. The compare-and-replace guarantee holds within one Registry instance.

legacy_keystore_fallback.problem: FileStore.load tested the error from building the candidate list instead of the error from os.ReadFile, so it accepted a path it had just failed to read and the pre-M4.1 kind-named layout could never be loaded at all
legacy_keystore_fallback.fix: success is now decided by lastErr from this os.ReadFile; a non-ENOENT failure is reported instead of silently falling back to the legacy file; a missing key reports a clear 'no key file' error

stale_rotation.problem: ApplyRotation did read-modify-Replace with no atomic precondition, so a stale rotation could overwrite a newer generation or roll the device backwards onto retired key material
stale_rotation.fix: Registry.CompareAndReplace validates generation + old sign key id + old agreement key id INSIDE the write lock and writes nothing on mismatch; Rotation.Validate requires ToGeneration == FromGeneration+1

reload_revision_rollback.problem: Reload read and parsed the file before taking the lock, then overwrote memory unconditionally, so it could write an older snapshot over a just-committed Replace
reload_revision_rollback.fix: the snapshot is adopted only if its revision is >= the in-memory revision (compare at publish); a stale snapshot is discarded, not an error

session_registry_capacity.problem: Register ran the MaxSessions check even when replacing the same device, so at full capacity a reconnect was refused while the defer had already closed the old session, leaving a closed session in the map
session_registry_capacity.fix: replacing the same device is a swap: it does not consume a slot and is not subject to MaxSessions; a new device is still an admission and is still bounded; the superseded session is closed outside the lock; the map ends up pointing at the new session

lifecycle_sweep_scope.problem: SweepRevoked inspected a session and then called Terminate(id), so it could kill a newer session that superseded the inspected one in between
lifecycle_sweep_scope.fix: SessionRegistry.TerminateIfCurrent(deviceID, expectedSession) only removes the exact SessionState that was inspected; both sweep paths use it, as does the superseded serve() teardown via UnregisterIfCurrent

registry_commit_failure_injection.problem: the M4.1 test never called a failing ApplyRotation, so it proved nothing about a failed commit
registry_commit_failure_injection.fix: Replace persists by writing <trust>.tmp then renaming; occupying <trust>.tmp with a directory makes os.WriteFile fail for real. ApplyRotation is then actually called and must fail
registry_commit_failure_injection.note: replacing the trust file itself with a regular file does NOT work -- the rename would overwrite it and the commit would appear to succeed
registry_commit_failure_injection.assertions: ApplyRotation returns an error; memory and disk still name generation N; N's private keys still load; the N+1 files exist but are referenced by no registry entry

wire_replay_evidence_fields.problem: channel fields were reported false although session B really did complete its handshake before the injection
wire_replay_evidence_fields.fix: device_channel_created=true, gateway_channel_created=true, plaintext_delivered=false, business_accepted=false, record_replay_accepted=false. Unobserved fields stay null, never guessed as false

manifest_and_docs.stale_starter_manifest: moved to docs/history/STARTER_MANIFEST.sha256 with a README stating it is historical and must not be used to verify; the project root no longer has a MANIFEST.sha256 that produces FAILED results
manifest_and_docs.delivery_manifest: the review package root MANIFEST.sha256 is the single valid delivery manifest
docs_synced: docs/PROTOCOL_DRAFT.md (v0.3: suite 2 implemented, default config runs)
docs/LIFECYCLE.md (rotation replaces BOTH key kinds; CAS and single-writer stated)

full_stream.counts: computed by the summarizer from the JSON stream, never pre-written

targeted_stream.purpose: convenience regression only; it does NOT back the project-wide pass total

verification_gaps: the race detector still cannot run on this machine (MinGW requests __iob_func, absent from msvcrt.dll); the concurrency tests are functional, NOT race-detector results
SM2 key agreement still has no independent implementation cross-check (OpenSSL exposes no SM2MQV)
reuse of an ML-KEM encapsulation key across sessions is not detectable by the responder
not_claimed: cross-process concurrent registry update safety (single-writer by policy only)
a post-quantum secure system (SM2 identity authentication is not post-quantum)
a security audit or compliance certification
may_proceed_note: M4.2 is complete. The two verification gaps are carried forward and must be closed before deployment or any claim of complete verification.
